description:
Retry backoff was `(1 <<< retry_count) + :rand.uniform(3)`: a ceiling that
doubles, with one to three milliseconds of jitter.

With N transactions contending on one key they fail at nearly the same
instant, compute nearly the same delay, and wake together -- so they
collide again and the round trip repeats at twice the delay. The work is
trivial; the wall clock is set by whichever contender climbs furthest up
the ladder.

MEASURED, 100 concurrent signups on one seat counter (the class-scheduling
demo's "dans" section), ten independent rounds:

  before: min=154.7 median=284.7 max=1058.0 total=4760.8ms
          min=281.4 median=540.1 max=3057.3 total=7161.1ms
          samples snap to a ladder: 280 / 540 / 1058 / 3057

  after:  min=168.6 median=209.5 max=387.1 total=2326.9ms
          min=150.5 median=201.7 max=320.3 total=2054.1ms

Tail 2.7-9.5x better; total 2-3.5x. The ladder is gone.

FIX: full jitter, which is what FDB's client does. The delay is a uniform
draw from the whole interval below the ceiling, and only the CEILING
grows (NativeAPI.actor.cpp:4436 `returnedBackoff *= random01()`, ceiling
grown at :4446 by BACKOFF_GROWTH_RATE; knobs ClientKnobs.cpp:67-69 --
10ms initial, 1s max, growth 2.0). The ceiling schedule is unchanged;
what changed is drawing from all of it instead of a 3ms band at the top.

Never zero, so a retry cannot become a spin.

NOT a regression: measured at 0.5.3 (198ms), 0.6.0 (150ms), 0.6.1-era
(283ms), pre-merge (277ms) and today (281ms). The schedule dates to
602f0c8a. It was always this way; it was simply never measured.

The ~200ms floor that remains is the real cost: 100 transactions
contending on one key must serialize, so ~2ms per commit x 100.
title: Retry backoff collides in lockstep: full jitter, FDB-style
